artworks.title: The Funeral of Patroclus
artworks.description: David's funeral pyre — Patroclus' body at the centre of Iliadic grief, the games and sacrifice that follow Hector's kill.

artworks.title: Achilles Bandaging the Wounded Patroclus
artworks.description: The Sosias Painter's cup — Achilles binding Patroclus' wound, the friendship Homeric art never stopped restaging before the fall.

artworks.title: Menelaus Bearing the Body of Patroclus (The Pasquino Group)
artworks.artist: Unknown (Roman copy after a Hellenistic original)
artworks.year: Roman period (after a 3rd-century BCE Greek bronze)
artworks.description: The Pasquino Group — Menelaus (or Ajax) bearing Patroclus' corpse, Hellenistic pathos that made the body's recovery a sculptural type.

artworks.title: Warriors Lifting the Body of Patroclus (Etruscan relief)
artworks.description: Etruscan relief of warriors lifting Patroclus — Italic reception of the Iliad's most mourned corpse.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Petersen's epic makes Patroclus' death in Achilles' armor the film's emotional hinge — the friend that brings the hero back to war.

popCulture.title: Patroclus
popCulture.description: The companion who dies wearing Achilles' arms — Book XVI's fall that turns the Iliad toward vengeance.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.description: Hector's slaying of Patroclus remains the poem's central grief — the death that costs Troy its best defender.

popCulture.title: The Song of Achilles
popCulture.creator: Madeline Miller
popCulture.description: Miller's novel retells the Iliad through Patroclus' love — his death in Achilles' armor as the book's devastating hinge.
